# Results — Study 685 (Tri-Star Doji) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**three dojis in a row mark a major reversal** — encoded as two honest cuts: a **strict**,
literature-faithful island tri-star (the middle doji's range clears both neighbours, the
gapped "star" shape Nison describes) and a **loose** cut (three dojis back to back, no gap
requirement, common enough to actually run inference on). Both are pinned against the
**unconditional base rate** — the same against-the-trend bet on every eligible bar. As-of
**2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).
Panel fingerprint `7c12cddbd539`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLCV, **61 names** (SPY + 60 long-listed US large-caps spanning every major sector), cache-first |
| Window | ~25.0 years per name, 2001-ish → 2026-06-30, **383,080** total daily bars |
| Sample fingerprint | SPY: `d1ac9e0ecaae` (6,280 rows, 2001-07-10 → 2026-06-30) |
| Detector | doji = body ≤ **10%** of the bar's high-low range (same cut as siblings 405/458); tri-star = three consecutive dojis |
| Execution / costs | tri-star confirmed on the close of the third doji; entered at the **next open** (one documented lag); reversal bet is against the 10-day move into the block; 2 bps round-trip + 1 bp borrow on the short leg |
| Statistics | Welch *t* of tri-star reversal mean vs the base-rate reversal mean (the decisive test); one-sample HAC *t* and a 2,000-draw label-shuffle placebo where n permits; **Bonferroni** correction across 4 horizons (critical \|*t*\| ≥ **2.50**); below **8** pooled events, no *t*-stat is computed at all — "too few to test," not a decorative number |

No survivorship on the Signal axis in the sense that matters here: this is a single-pattern
event study (not a cross-sectional portfolio), so a fixed, currently-liquid basket affects
which *names* contribute events, not the direction of the reversal-vs-base-rate comparison.

## The detector — how rare is "three dojis in a row", really?

| cut | definition | count (pooled, 61 names, 25y) |
|---|---|--:|
| **Strict** (literature-faithful) | 3 consecutive dojis, middle bar's range clears both neighbours (a true gapped island star) | **2** |
| **Loose** (plain reading) | 3 consecutive dojis, no gap requirement | **410** |

The lore's own emphasis on rarity is *earned*: demanding the actual gapped "star" shape
collapses 410 candidate three-doji blocks down to **two** in a quarter-century across 61
liquid large-caps. That is the honest starting point — and it caps what any statistic below
can possibly certify.

## Strict cut — the literature-faithful island tri-star (n = 2, too few to test)

| horizon | n | mean reversal return | win rate | test |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| 5d  | 2 | **−243.0 bps** | 0% | *not computed — n < 8* |
| 10d | 2 | **−249.6 bps** | 0% | *not computed — n < 8* |
| 20d | 2 | **−610.6 bps** | 0% | *not computed — n < 8* |
| 60d | 2 | **−1,355.3 bps** | 0% | *not computed — n < 8* |

The two real occurrences: **JPM**, tri-star ending 2021-03-19 (block 2021-03-17→19, after an
up-move — the claim says "sell"), 60-day reversal return **−215.6 bps (−2.16%)** — the
"reversal" lost as JPM kept climbing; and **CSCO**, tri-star ending 2019-01-28 (block
2019-01-24→28, also after an up-move), 60-day reversal return **−2,495.1 bps (−24.95%)** —
CSCO's early-2019 rally simply continued straight through the "major reversal" signal. Two
trades, two losses.
This is a **description**, not a statistic — n = 2 cannot support a t-test — but it is the
honest, complete record of the pattern precisely as the literature defines it.

## Loose cut — three dojis in a row, no gap requirement (the honest power check)

Bonferroni-corrected critical \|*t*\| for 4 simultaneous horizons: **2.50**.

| horizon | n | tri-star mean | win% | base rate | delta (tri − base) | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5d  | 410 | −14.3 bps | 48% | +2.1 bps | **−16.4 bps** | −1.02 | 0.826 |
| 10d | 410 | −19.1 bps | 47% | +1.9 bps | **−20.9 bps** | −0.98 | 0.807 |
| 20d | 410 | −76.6 bps | 44% | +6.2 bps | **−82.8 bps** | −2.47 | 0.986 |
| 60d | 410 | −86.7 bps | 46% | +7.5 bps | **−94.1 bps** | −1.65 | 0.933 |

**No horizon clears the Bonferroni bar** (the closest, 20d at Welch *t* = −2.47, still falls
short of 2.50 — and it is negative, the *wrong* sign for the claim in any case). The tri-star
reversal bet **underperforms the base rate at every single horizon**, by 16 to 94 bps, and a
label-shuffle placebo confirms it: a random same-size set of bars beats the tri-star mean
**81–99% of the time**. If a tri-star means anything at all on this reading, it points toward
*continuation*, not reversal — though even that reading does not clear the desk's bar.

## Costs — net of 2 bps round-trip + 1 bp borrow on the short leg (loose cut)

| horizon | gross (bps) | net (bps) |
|---|--:|--:|
| 5d  | −14.3 | −16.8 |
| 10d | −19.1 | −21.6 |
| 20d | −76.6 | −79.1 |
| 60d | −86.7 | −89.2 |

There is no gross edge to defend, so costs only make an already-losing bet worse.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic panel: 40 names, ~13.9 years each, forced 3-bar doji blocks at a controlled
rate with a TUNABLE planted reversal (knob `edge`); no network. The decisive statistic is the
same Welch *t* of tri-star mean vs base-rate mean used on the real tape.

| world | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.60** (sd 1.16), \|*t*\| ≥ 2 in **4/20** seeds |
| planted edge = 0.02 (seed 685) | delta **+52.9 bps**, Welch *t* = **+2.36** |
| planted edge = 0.04 (seed 685) | delta **+129.3 bps**, Welch *t* = **+5.14** |

Two things to say plainly. First, the null is **not** perfectly calibrated at the textbook
5%: forcing three artificially low-variance days into a random walk leaves a small residual
(mean *t* ≈ −0.6, a mild negative lean, firing on 4/20 seeds instead of ~1/20) — a known,
named quirk of this synthetic generator, not a claim about the market. Second, and
decisively, that residual is tiny next to what the detector needs to *plant and recover*: an
`edge` of just 0.02–0.04 (an order of magnitude below the swings the real tape shows) lights
up cleanly at *t* = +2.36 and +5.14. Per the desk's standing rule, **a synthetic control never
backs a Signal stamp** — it exists only to prove the harness can find a real, planted effect,
which it demonstrably can; the honest, unglamorous real-tape result above stands on its own.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The literature-faithful strict tri-star fires only **twice** in 61
  names × 25 years — both times the "major reversal" lost money (mean −611 to −1,355 bps
  depending on horizon, 0% win rate), too few to test formally. The loose, common-enough-to-test
  cut (n = 410) shows the reversal bet **losing to the base rate at every horizon** (−16 to
  −94 bps), and no horizon clears the Bonferroni-corrected bar (\|*t*\| ≥ 2.50) — the closest,
  20d, is −2.47, short of the bar **and the wrong sign**. There is no certified reversal signal
  here, in either the rare or the common reading.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The literature-faithful pattern occurs roughly **once per 30
  ticker-years** — not a strategy, a curiosity. Even granting the loose reading, there is no
  gross edge to defend: net of a 2 bps round-trip and short borrow, every horizon loses more
  than it did gross.
- **"Does the tri-star mark a major reversal?" — BUSTED.** Both real strict occurrences lost;
  the loose cut's delta is negative at every horizon; the label-shuffle placebo shows a random
  same-size sample beats the tri-star 81–99% of the time. Stacking three dojis instead of one
  does not manufacture a reversal that a single doji ([study 405](../../405-doji-reversal/))
  already failed to show.
